speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have experienced shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To understand what might be causing this, have you noticed any drainage, hearing loss, or dizziness since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing that history; since you have chronic ear infections and pain when eating or wearing earrings, have you noticed any fluid leaking from the ear or a sensation of fullness?

REQUEST TEST: Audiogram (to verify current hearing status and rule out ossicular chain issues).

speaker: Doctor
text: The audiogram results show normal readings, so hearing loss isn't the cause. Given your pain when eating and wearing earrings, could you describe if you feel pressure in the middle ear or notice any clicking sounds when you chew?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The connection between your pain and eating suggests involvement of the middle ear muscles, specifically the stapedius or tensor tympani. Given your history of chronic infections and recent surgery, have you noticed a sensation of fullness or tinnitus, and does the pain get worse when you clench your jaw or move your head?

REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT of the Temporal Bone.
REQUEST IMAGES: Coronal and Axial views focusing on the middle ear muscles and ossicular chain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain radiating from eating and the specific discomfort with earrings strongly suggest tensor tympani spasm or myofascial pain involving the tensor tympani and masticatory muscles. Has the pain ever been relieved by resting your jaw or applying pressure to the jawline?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myofascial Pain Syndrome of the Tensor Tympani and Masticatory Muscles
